method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from World Health Organization 'Guidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV' (2022 (issued 23 June 2022; replaces the 2018 guidelines)), 22 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO (read at the copyright page of the PDF at https://iris.who.int/server/api/core/bitstreams/f5954a67-f604-4442-bb2f-5bb06894c791/content). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Chang CC, Harrison TS, Bicanic TA, et al., European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM), International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (ISHAM) and American Society for Microbiology (ASM), Lancet Infect Dis 24(8):e495-e512 (doi 10.1016/S1473-3099(23)00731-4); author manuscript NIHMS2026967 'Global guideline for the diagnosis and management of cryptococcosis: an initiative of the ECMM and ISHAM in cooperation with the ASM' (2024 (online 9 February 2024)), 12 claims; LICENCE: © Elsevier (author manuscript). PMC statement: 'This file is available for text mining. It may also be used consistent with the principles of fair use under the copyright law.' (read at NCBI efetch JATS XML <permissions> element for PMC11526416 (Europe PMC returned HTTP 500 for the full text)). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 adds S2, the 2024 ECMM/ISHAM/ASM global cryptococcosis guideline, read as the NIH author manuscript in PMC and paraphrased; the S1 claims are unchanged. The Australasian cryptococcosis consensus (Intern Med J 2021, doi 10.1111/imj.15590) was retried first and Wiley again returned HTTP 403. S2's regimen tables and figures (Table 2, Figures 1-2) are not in the manuscript text.

claims.claim: **Meningitis is the dominant form,** making up as much as 90% of cryptococcal disease linked to HIV; the infection is rare in children with HIV.
claims.locator: World Health Organization, 'Guidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV', 2022 (issued 23 June 2022; replaces the 2018 guidelines), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/357088, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Suspected first episode: do a lumbar puncture promptly,** measuring CSF opening pressure and running a rapid cryptococcal antigen test (strong recommendation). Send CSF for fungal culture at the same time where feasible.
claims.locator: World Health Organization, 'Guidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV', 2022 (issued 23 June 2022; replaces the 2018 guidelines), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/357088, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If lumbar puncture is unavailable or contraindicated,** a rapid antigen test on serum, plasma or whole blood (result within 24 hours) is preferred; without one, refer promptly for work-up and treatment.
claims.locator: World Health Organization, 'Guidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV', 2022 (issued 23 June 2022; replaces the 2018 guidelines), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/357088, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Raised intracranial pressure is not a reason to avoid lumbar puncture here.** The contraindications are significant coagulopathy, a suspected space-occupying lesion (focal signs other than a sixth-nerve palsy, or recurrent seizures, ideally confirmed on CT), major spinal deformity and informed refusal.
claims.locator: World Health Organization, 'Guidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV', 2022 (issued 23 June 2022; replaces the 2018 guidelines), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/357088, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Screen for cryptococcal antigen before starting or restarting ART when CD4 is below 100 cells/mm³,** and treat antigen-positive people pre-emptively (strong). A threshold below 200 may be considered (conditional).
claims.locator: World Health Organization, 'Guidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV', 2022 (issued 23 June 2022; replaces the 2018 guidelines), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/357088, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Every antigen-positive person needs assessment for meningitis,** with lumbar puncture where feasible. India ink misses cases, so confirm a negative India ink with CSF antigen testing or culture.
claims.locator: World Health Organization, 'Guidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV', 2022 (issued 23 June 2022; replaces the 2018 guidelines), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/357088, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pre-emptive therapy for antigen-positive screening:** fluconazole 800–1200 mg/day in adults (12 mg/kg per day in adolescents) for two weeks, then consolidation and maintenance fluconazole exactly as for treatment.
claims.locator: World Health Organization, 'Guidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV', 2022 (issued 23 June 2022; replaces the 2018 guidelines), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/357088, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Where antigen screening is not available,** give adults and adolescents with CD4 below 100 cells/mm³ fluconazole primary prophylaxis instead (strong).
claims.locator: World Health Organization, 'Guidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV', 2022 (issued 23 June 2022; replaces the 2018 guidelines), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/357088, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Preferred induction (new in this edition):** one dose of liposomal amphotericin B at 10 mg/kg, plus flucytosine 100 mg/kg daily split into four doses for 14 days, plus fluconazole — 1200 mg daily in adults, or 12 mg/kg daily (up to 800 mg) in children and adolescents (strong).
claims.locator: World Health Organization, 'Guidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV', 2022 (issued 23 June 2022; replaces the 2018 guidelines), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/357088, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Without liposomal amphotericin:** amphotericin B deoxycholate 1 mg/kg daily with flucytosine 100 mg/kg daily (four divided doses) for seven days, then seven days of fluconazole at the induction dose.
claims.locator: World Health Organization, 'Guidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV', 2022 (issued 23 June 2022; replaces the 2018 guidelines), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/357088, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Without any amphotericin:** 14 days of oral fluconazole 1200 mg daily plus flucytosine 100 mg/kg daily. It is the only oral combination WHO endorses, and it carried lower mortality than deoxycholate amphotericin with fluconazole.
claims.locator: World Health Organization, 'Guidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV', 2022 (issued 23 June 2022; replaces the 2018 guidelines), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/357088, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Without flucytosine:** give fluconazole 1200 mg daily with either liposomal amphotericin B at 3–4 mg/kg daily or deoxycholate amphotericin at 1 mg/kg daily, for 14 days. Regimens that include flucytosine work better, so access to it should be secured.
claims.locator: World Health Organization, 'Guidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV', 2022 (issued 23 June 2022; replaces the 2018 guidelines), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/357088, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not give routine adjunctive corticosteroids during induction** (strong). In the trial, dexamethasone did not lower mortality, added disability and serious adverse events, and slowed CSF fungal clearance.
claims.locator: World Health Organization, 'Guidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV', 2022 (issued 23 June 2022; replaces the 2018 guidelines), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/357088, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consolidation:** fluconazole 800 mg daily in adults (6–12 mg/kg per day in children and adolescents, maximum 800 mg) for eight weeks after induction.
claims.locator: World Health Organization, 'Guidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV', 2022 (issued 23 June 2022; replaces the 2018 guidelines), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/357088, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Maintenance:** fluconazole 200 mg daily in adults (6 mg/kg per day in children and adolescents) until the immune system recovers — CD4 above 200 cells/mm³ with a suppressed viral load on ART (strong, high certainty).
claims.locator: World Health Organization, 'Guidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV', 2022 (issued 23 June 2022; replaces the 2018 guidelines), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/357088, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not start ART straight away:** early ART raised mortality, so defer it 4–6 weeks from the start of antifungals — four weeks after an amphotericin-based induction, 4–6 weeks after fluconazole with flucytosine.
claims.locator: World Health Organization, 'Guidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV', 2022 (issued 23 June 2022; replaces the 2018 guidelines), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/357088, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Everyone with suspected cryptococcal meningitis gets an initial and an early repeat lumbar puncture with opening pressure,** whether or not they have symptoms of raised pressure.
claims.locator: World Health Organization, 'Guidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV', 2022 (issued 23 June 2022; replaces the 2018 guidelines), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/357088, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Therapeutic lumbar puncture:** drain enough CSF to bring the pressure under 20 cm H₂O, or to half the baseline if it is very high (20–30 mL is usually enough). Repeat daily while symptoms persist, until they resolve or the pressure has been normal for at least two days.
claims.locator: World Health Organization, 'Guidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV', 2022 (issued 23 June 2022; replaces the 2018 guidelines), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/357088, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Review the clinical response every day for the first two weeks of induction.** Antigen titres in CSF, serum or plasma should not be used to monitor response in any setting.
claims.locator: World Health Organization, 'Guidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV', 2022 (issued 23 June 2022; replaces the 2018 guidelines), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/357088, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **On relapse:** restart induction, relieve raised pressure by therapeutic lumbar puncture, reinforce adherence, begin ART after 4–6 weeks of effective antifungals if not already on it, and test fluconazole susceptibility where possible.
claims.locator: World Health Organization, 'Guidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV', 2022 (issued 23 June 2022; replaces the 2018 guidelines), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/357088, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Think of cryptococcosis in anyone with compatible symptoms or microbiology, whatever their immune status;** if there is no known predisposition, test for HIV and check a CD4 count.
claims.locator: Chang CC, Harrison TS, Bicanic TA, et al., European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM), International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (ISHAM) and American Society for Microbiology (ASM), Lancet Infect Dis 24(8):e495-e512 (doi 10.1016/S1473-3099(23)00731-4); author manuscript NIHMS2026967, 'Global guideline for the diagnosis and management of cryptococcosis: an initiative of the ECMM and ISHAM in cooperation with the ASM', 2024 (online 9 February 2024), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11526416/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Look for spread in every case, including antigenaemia alone:** lumbar puncture with opening pressure, cell count, glucose, protein, microscopy, culture and CSF antigen titre; blood antigen titre and cultures of blood, sputum and other sites; ideally brain MRI and chest CT.
claims.locator: Chang CC, Harrison TS, Bicanic TA, et al., European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM), International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (ISHAM) and American Society for Microbiology (ASM), Lancet Infect Dis 24(8):e495-e512 (doi 10.1016/S1473-3099(23)00731-4); author manuscript NIHMS2026967, 'Global guideline for the diagnosis and management of cryptococcosis: an initiative of the ECMM and ISHAM in cooperation with the ASM', 2024 (online 9 February 2024), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11526416/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Induction differs by setting.** In resource-rich settings the usual standard is liposomal amphotericin B 3–4 mg/kg daily plus flucytosine (25 mg/kg, given four times daily) for 2 weeks, not the single 10 mg/kg dose that S1 prefers. The African trials behind S1's regimen are disputed as a guide for well-resourced care and for people without HIV, where no data exist.
claims.locator: Chang CC, Harrison TS, Bicanic TA, et al., European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM), International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (ISHAM) and American Society for Microbiology (ASM), Lancet Infect Dis 24(8):e495-e512 (doi 10.1016/S1473-3099(23)00731-4); author manuscript NIHMS2026967, 'Global guideline for the diagnosis and management of cryptococcosis: an initiative of the ECMM and ISHAM in cooperation with the ASM', 2024 (online 9 February 2024), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11526416/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Transplant recipients:** cryptococcosis is their third most common invasive fungal infection. Blood antigen can be negative, especially with a single lung nodule. Lipid amphotericin was linked to lower mortality than deoxycholate for CNS disease, and the AMBITION regimen is untested without HIV.
claims.locator: Chang CC, Harrison TS, Bicanic TA, et al., European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM), International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (ISHAM) and American Society for Microbiology (ASM), Lancet Infect Dis 24(8):e495-e512 (doi 10.1016/S1473-3099(23)00731-4); author manuscript NIHMS2026967, 'Global guideline for the diagnosis and management of cryptococcosis: an initiative of the ECMM and ISHAM in cooperation with the ASM', 2024 (online 9 February 2024), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11526416/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Outside HIV, S2 advises against routine blood antigen screening, and against primary prophylaxis or pre-emptive treatment.** In HIV, S2 screens below a CD4 of 200 and treats asymptomatic antigenaemia (after a lumbar puncture excludes meningitis) with fluconazole 1200 mg daily for 2 weeks, 800 mg daily for 8 weeks, then 200 mg for about 6 months.
claims.locator: Chang CC, Harrison TS, Bicanic TA, et al., European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM), International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (ISHAM) and American Society for Microbiology (ASM), Lancet Infect Dis 24(8):e495-e512 (doi 10.1016/S1473-3099(23)00731-4); author manuscript NIHMS2026967, 'Global guideline for the diagnosis and management of cryptococcosis: an initiative of the ECMM and ISHAM in cooperation with the ASM', 2024 (online 9 February 2024), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11526416/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Pulmonary disease:** treat as meningitis if there is fungaemia, CNS involvement, a blood antigen titre of 1:512 or more by latex agglutination (or about 10-fold higher by lateral flow), or severe lung disease. Mild isolated lung disease without a cryptococcoma has responded to fluconazole 400 mg daily.
claims.locator: Chang CC, Harrison TS, Bicanic TA, et al., European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM), International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (ISHAM) and American Society for Microbiology (ASM), Lancet Infect Dis 24(8):e495-e512 (doi 10.1016/S1473-3099(23)00731-4); author manuscript NIHMS2026967, 'Global guideline for the diagnosis and management of cryptococcosis: an initiative of the ECMM and ISHAM in cooperation with the ASM', 2024 (online 9 February 2024), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11526416/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ***C. gattii*** (seen mostly in apparently immunocompetent people): treat as for *C. neoformans*, but consider 4–6 weeks of induction for CNS disease without HIV, and shunt early for obstructive hydrocephalus. Some lateral flow antigen tests miss it.
claims.locator: Chang CC, Harrison TS, Bicanic TA, et al., European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM), International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (ISHAM) and American Society for Microbiology (ASM), Lancet Infect Dis 24(8):e495-e512 (doi 10.1016/S1473-3099(23)00731-4); author manuscript NIHMS2026967, 'Global guideline for the diagnosis and management of cryptococcosis: an initiative of the ECMM and ISHAM in cooperation with the ASM', 2024 (online 9 February 2024), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11526416/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Raised pressure:** measure opening pressure at every lumbar puncture and image the brain to exclude obstructed CSF outflow; schedule a therapeutic tap at about 48–72 hours and/or day 7 whatever the first pressure. If symptomatic pressure persists despite taps, use a lumbar drain, shunt or ventriculostomy.
claims.locator: Chang CC, Harrison TS, Bicanic TA, et al., European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM), International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (ISHAM) and American Society for Microbiology (ASM), Lancet Infect Dis 24(8):e495-e512 (doi 10.1016/S1473-3099(23)00731-4); author manuscript NIHMS2026967, 'Global guideline for the diagnosis and management of cryptococcosis: an initiative of the ECMM and ISHAM in cooperation with the ASM', 2024 (online 9 February 2024), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11526416/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **ART timing:** never immediate. With suboptimal antifungals, delay 4–6 weeks (as S1); in resource-rich settings with optimal treatment, individualise (usually 4–6 weeks) by clinical and pressure response, CSF sterility and co-infections, aiming for culture-negative CSF first. Isolated lung disease or antigenaemia alone may allow ART earlier, for example at 2 weeks.
claims.locator: Chang CC, Harrison TS, Bicanic TA, et al., European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM), International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (ISHAM) and American Society for Microbiology (ASM), Lancet Infect Dis 24(8):e495-e512 (doi 10.1016/S1473-3099(23)00731-4); author manuscript NIHMS2026967, 'Global guideline for the diagnosis and management of cryptococcosis: an initiative of the ECMM and ISHAM in cooperation with the ASM', 2024 (online 9 February 2024), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11526416/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Suspected C-IRIS:** first exclude relapse and other causes (MRI brain, lumbar puncture). Treat with therapeutic taps and symptom control, keep the antifungal, and do not stop ART. For persistent symptoms despite taps, prednisolone about 0.5–1.0 mg/kg daily or dexamethasone about 0.2–0.3 mg/kg daily, tapered over 4–6 weeks, may be considered.
claims.locator: Chang CC, Harrison TS, Bicanic TA, et al., European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM), International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (ISHAM) and American Society for Microbiology (ASM), Lancet Infect Dis 24(8):e495-e512 (doi 10.1016/S1473-3099(23)00731-4); author manuscript NIHMS2026967, 'Global guideline for the diagnosis and management of cryptococcosis: an initiative of the ECMM and ISHAM in cooperation with the ASM', 2024 (online 9 February 2024), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11526416/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Culture-positive relapse or persistence:** test antifungal susceptibility on the first and relapse isolates side by side; a rise in fluconazole MIC of more than 2 dilutions suggests emerging resistance. Do not escalate treatment for persistent antigen, visible yeasts without growth, or abnormal CSF chemistry alone.
claims.locator: Chang CC, Harrison TS, Bicanic TA, et al., European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM), International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (ISHAM) and American Society for Microbiology (ASM), Lancet Infect Dis 24(8):e495-e512 (doi 10.1016/S1473-3099(23)00731-4); author manuscript NIHMS2026967, 'Global guideline for the diagnosis and management of cryptococcosis: an initiative of the ECMM and ISHAM in cooperation with the ASM', 2024 (online 9 February 2024), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11526416/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Pregnancy (S2 is firmer than S1):** use amphotericin (liposomal or deoxycholate) through induction, consolidation and maintenance and for antigenaemia; avoid flucytosine and fluconazole, especially in the first trimester. Fluconazole can be used after delivery.
claims.locator: Chang CC, Harrison TS, Bicanic TA, et al., European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM), International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (ISHAM) and American Society for Microbiology (ASM), Lancet Infect Dis 24(8):e495-e512 (doi 10.1016/S1473-3099(23)00731-4); author manuscript NIHMS2026967, 'Global guideline for the diagnosis and management of cryptococcosis: an initiative of the ECMM and ISHAM in cooperation with the ASM', 2024 (online 9 February 2024), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11526416/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Pregnancy:** amphotericin B may be used when benefit outweighs harm. Fluconazole and flucytosine have been linked to birth defects in animal and some uncontrolled human studies, so weigh their use case by case.
claims.locator: World Health Organization, 'Guidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV', 2022 (issued 23 June 2022; replaces the 2018 guidelines), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/357088, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Localised disease outside the meninges:** a suggested (expert-opinion) course is fluconazole at 800 mg/day for two weeks, stepping to 400 mg/day for eight weeks, then 200 mg/day as maintenance. Disseminated disease shown by a positive blood culture is treated as meningitis.
claims.locator: World Health Organization, 'Guidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV', 2022 (issued 23 June 2022; replaces the 2018 guidelines), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/357088, retrieved 2026-09-23
